exposure: Somatic, endocrine, and reproductive health disorders
outcome: Mental and neurotic disorders of an anxiety-phobic nature
Planned and urgent surgical delivery by cesarean section
cohort: The study included 15,448 women who gave birth in Lviv Hospital District during 2024 (martial law period), compared to 19,113 women who gave birth in 2021 (pre-war period).
finding: During martial law, war-related stress significantly increased the incidence of mental/neurotic disorders in pregnant women and led to a rise in labor complications including intranatal distress, abnormal labor activity, placental abruption, uterine bleeding, preeclampsia progression, septic complications, and preterm birth.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean section increased by 2.2% during martial law, attributed to the deterioration of maternal somatic and reproductive health, increased age and parity, more intrapartum complications, and a concentration of internally displaced pregnant women with uterine scars.
cross-section timing: Data was collected for two distinct periods: 2024 (during martial law) and 2021 (pre-war).
